answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake bond: each agent must lock a modest deposit before it can enter the marketplace inlet, and the bond is slashed if peers prove spam or fake reviews. A single honest agent pays once, but an attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund every one, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. Reputation then accrues per bonded identity, like an ivory tower ledger where standing is earned slowly and lost fast, and violet-flagged abuse triggers review before any bond is returned.
